You need to move the toolhead to where the work origin will be, and tap Run Boundary to check the work area of the current position.
You need to separately set origin in each orientation, and their combination will be the work origin. You can tap Run Boundary to check the work area in the X and Y orientations.

Fix the material to the CNC carving and cutting platform. Manually move the toolhead to the position that you want to set as the work origin. The CNC job will start with the defined origin. You can tap Run Boundary to check the work area of the current position.

Manually move the toolhead to the position that you want to set as the work origin. The laser job will start with the defined origin. You can tap Run Boundary to check the work area of the current position.

Move the toolhead (the center of the crosshairs) to the desired position for the XY work origin, based on which the laser job will start. \nYou can tap Run Boundary to verify the work area for the current origin.

Move the toolhead (the center of the crosshairs) to the desired position for the XY work origin, based on which the laser job will start. \nYou can tap Run Boundary to verify the work area for the current origin.

Place the material on the laser engraving and cutting platform, and then put the laser calibration target on top of the material. Manually lower the toolhead towards the calibration target’s surface until you feel slight resistance when you pull out the calibration target. Tap Next, and the machine will adjust the laser height automatically.
Manually move the toolhead until the laser beam is focused into the smallest spot possible. Tap Next, and the machine will use the current height as the laser height.
Measure and enter the material thickness. Then, place the material on the laser engraving and cutting platform. The machine will adjust the laser height accordingly.

1. Fix the material and put the calibration card on top of the material. \n2. Lower the focus lever to touch the card until you feel slight resistance when moving the card. \n3. Tap Next, then retract and lock the focus lever.
The Enclosure door is opened, so the %s has been stopped.

If you have set the work origin using Origin Assistant, as long as the dimensions of the material remain unchanged, you can skip this step and start the job right away.
Input the material thickness. Then, the machine will adjust the laser height.
Lower the toolhead against the material surface. Then, the machine will adjust the laser height.
Manually adjust the laser height. The machine use the current height of the toolhead to start the job.
Measure and input the material’s diameter. Then, fix the material to the 3-jaw chuck. The machine will adjust the laser height based on the material diameter.
1. Measure and input the material’s diameter. \n2. Fix the material to the 3-jaw chuck. \n3. Tap Next.

Fix the material to the 3-jaw chuck. Adjust the height of the toolhead until the laser beam is focused into the smallest spot on the material surface. Tap Next, and the machine will use the current height as the laser height.
Fix the material to the 3-jaw chuck. Lower the toolhead against the material’s top surface. Based on the given focal length, the machine will adjust the laser height.

1. Place the calibration card on top of the material. \n2. Lower the focus lever to touch the card until you feel slight resistance when moving the card. \n3. Tap Next, then retract and lock the focus lever.

1. Place the calibration card on top of the material. \n2. Lower the focus lever to touch the card until you feel slight resistance when moving the card. \n3. Tap Next, then retract and lock the focus lever.

Manually move the toolhead to the position that you want to set as the work origin. The laser job will start with the defined origin. You can tap Run Boundary to check the work area of the current position.
How to Use the Focus Lever

Turn the knob to loosen or lock the focus lever. When the lever touches the material: if aligned with Scale 0, the laser will focus on the material surface; if aligned with other scales, the focal point will move deeper inside the material.
Turn the knob to loosen or lock the focus lever. When the lever touches the material: if aligned with Focus, the laser will focus on the material surface.
Are you sure to stop the job?
Don’t remove the print until the bed cools down under 40℃.
Are you sure to pause the job?
When you increase the Z Offset, the heated bed will descend, and vice versa.
The extruders will move into position later for you to load or unload the filament.
Step 2: Hang the filament onto the filament holder, and feed the filament into the guide tube until it reaches the other end.
Step 3: Push the toggle backward and hold; then insert the filament into the filament entry until you feel resistance (taking the left extruder for example).
Step 4: Set a target temperature and tap Heat.
Step 5: Tap Load until the filament oozes out of the nozzle (the extruder will automatically move to an appropriate position to start loading, if necessary).
Step 7: Insert the guide tube into the extruder and then snap it into the tube clip. Finally, reinstall the top panel.
